newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-CORK PULLS OUT OF ENGLAND TOUR OF ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CORK PULLS OUT OF ENGLAND TOUR OF ZIMBABWE.

text.p: England's prospects for their imminent tour of Zimbabwe were dented on Friday when Derbyshire strike bowler Dominic Cork withdrew from the squad.
Cork said he was pulling out for personal reasons and would join the party on the second leg of the tour in New Zealand.
The England management have not named a replacement and will rely on exisiting squad members to cover for Cork, one of the side's key players over the past two seasons.
"I have some personal matters that need to be resolved and I need some time to do it," Cork said on Friday.

"I was looking forward to going to Zimbabwe but I feel I wouldn't be able to concentrate on my cricket until I have resolved my personal problems, and obviously may not have been able to perform at my best."
Cork has taken 67 wickets in his 16 tests at an average of 29.08 runs since his impressive test debut in 1995, when he claimed seven for 43 to help England beat the West Indies at Lord's.
He took a total of 22 wickets in the two three-match series against India and Pakistan earlier ths year.
Surrey batsman Graham Thorpe will be another absentee when England fly out to Zimbabwe on Monday. His wife gave birth to a son last Wednesday. Thorpe will join the squad next Thursday.
